text:
sam: Quick thread: onboarding flagged multiple confusing examples about error handling. Folks are reading raw status codes and header strings. Can we converge on a small, stable JSON error envelope from the platform and a tiny SDK surface so sample apps behave the same across languages?

keiko: Yes. Current field spread: sometimes we get `message`, sometimes `error`, sometimes nested `details`. Suggest a single envelope shape for new endpoints: `{ code, message, http_status, retry_hint?, metadata? }` where `retry_hint` is machine-only and optional. Prefer this over heuristics in SDKs.

arjun: Love that. For parity, SDKs should map `code` -> typed exception class (e.g., "rate_limit" -> RateLimitError) and expose `retryHint` + `rawMetadata` fields. Also include `httpStatus` and original `headers` on the error for debugging.

leah: Small UX rule: keep the human `message` short (one sentence) and push operational guidance into `retry_hint` and `metadata`. That avoids people writing brittle parsers. Example: `{ code: "rate_limit", message: "Too many requests", http_status: 429, retry_hint: "retry-after", metadata: {quota_window: "minute"}}`.

sam: How about recommended enum values for `retry_hint`: `no-retry`, `retry-after`, `exponential`, `refresh-token`? SDKs implement a precedence: prefer explicit `retry_hint` in body, else parse `Retry-After` header, else fallback to heuristic by status.

keiko: Agreed. Also let's be explicit about `Retry-After: 0` meaning immediate retry. That has bitten teams.

arjun: For Go please export concrete error types and provide helpers `IsRetryable(err error) bool`, `RetryAfter(err error) time.Duration`, and `RetryHint(err error) string`. TS/py should support `instanceof` style checks and expose `err.retryAfter`.

infra-bot: telemetry note: would be great if the envelope included a `support_id` GUID so users can paste it into tickets and we can align logs. e.g. `support_id: "xxxx"` in `metadata`.

leah: +1 on support_id. Also propose including `internal_hint` in metadata for transient-vs-permanent, useful for SRE dashboards but not for user-facing copy. SDKs should not expose that field as first-class, but keep it in `raw` for debugging.

arjun: One tricky part is 5xx semantics. Sometimes we want automatic retry for 502/503, but 500 might be permanent for some models (OOM). Suggest the platform set `retry_hint` explicitly for 5xx where possible; otherwise SDKs default to `exponential` for 502/503 and `no-retry` for 500 unless `retry_hint` says otherwise. Document this mapping in onboarding.

sam: Nice. Action items: 1) platform: standardize envelope for new endpoints and include `retry_hint` + `support_id` when available; 2) SDKs: map code->typed errors, implement retry helpers and parse `Retry-After` (seconds or HTTP-date), treat 0 as immediate; 3) docs: update quickstarts to show `IsRetryable`/`RetryAfter` usage instead of raw status checks; 4) sample-apps: add lint to flag `err.status === 429` or equivalent.

keiko: I'll draft a short errors.md snippet for onboarding: mapping table + sample snippets for TS/Go/Py.

arjun: I'll open a small go PR exporting typed errors and helpers, plus tests for `Retry-After: 0`, numeric and HTTP-date forms, and body `retry_hint`.

leah: I'll add the linter rule to sample-apps CI. Also add an example showing how to attach `support_id` in support tickets.

infra-bot: CI note: please include a unit test in SDKs that ensures `err.rawHeaders` preserves casing for `Retry-After` so parsing works across mocks.

sam: Thanks all. This should reduce a lot of friction for new users. Putting this on the devex board as `errors: standard envelope + sdk helpers` and assigning owners. :white_check_mark:
